transcript: The muppets are making their Broadway debut, which of course means they get headshots and BIOS in the playbills. So here's a look at all of their BIOS. Kermit the frog is excited for this leap to the Broadway stage. Producer host of The Muppet Show, returning in 2026. Actor The Muppet Movie, The Muppet Christmas Carol, Muppet Treasure Island, Muppets Haunted Mansion and more. Author before you leap, he would like to thank all of the muppets, his 2,353 brothers and sisters, the lovers, the dreamers, and you for the continued support. Follow Kermit on social media. Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy would like to thank all her adoring fans for coming to see her in the Broadway spotlight where she belongs. Fashionista, model, diva, singer, black belt, karate, black belt designer, star of stage, screen and everywhere in between. You know her, and if you don't, why are you here? For your consideration in all Tony categories. Kissy Kissy follow. Mwah! Real Miss Piggy, the Great Gonzo. Greetings, culture lovers. The Great Gonzo has been performing artistic exploits and feats of lunatic daring since The Muppet Show. Can't wait to wow the huipil of Broadway. He has previously defied death live in front of thousands of legal witnesses at the Hollywood Bowl and the O2 Arena in London. He would like to dedicate this performance to all the chickens in the world, but most importantly, Camilla. Fozzie Bear can barely contain his excitement to join the show. He asks The audience to turn off their cell phones, laugh at the punchlines, and please, please do not heckle the performers, especially the comedian bear. This one is for Ma. The great laughers of the world and the Broadhurst Theater security team for keeping Statler and Waldorf out. Animal is the drummer of the Electric Mayhem. Editors note this was all we could get out of him. Ralph the dog. More than a piano player. Ralph got his start as the spokesperson for dog food commercials before rocketing to fame on variety shows in the 1960s. Then he was in some movies and other television shows. Now he's on Broadway. Not bad for a dog, huh
